claims.text: A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the target of the 'Provider support policy' link on the support index page).
The Pulumi provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Pulumi provides long-term security updates for some providers, and the provider support policy page identifies which providers get them.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The page /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists and lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry at /registry/ shows the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes during an update if an error occurs; it completes pending operations then exits and reports the error.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies desired state in a single step.
Pulumi native providers are mapped directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Experimental Pulumi features are always opt-in, enabled via a flag, command, or environment variable such as PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving long-term support updates are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, covering CVEs in the provider's code or direct dependencies, and fixes for broken internal infrastructure needed to ship them.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS providers remain compatible with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at unless security fixes require otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.
When N+1 ships, N becomes current-major-1 as the new LTS major, and the old LTS major reaches end of life the same day regardless of remaining 12-month window.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning to a major is recommended.
Older majors than the LTS version receive no patches; if v3 is newest, v2 is N-1 and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) ships new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
End-of-life versions (N-2 and older) are not supported and receive no updates.
Link targets exist: /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ anchor on best practices for maintaining provider versions, /registry/, /docs/support/getting-support/, and the registry package pages.
